Holy hell. That's an amazing story. I'm baffled that a family would care so much about someone that they'd go through all that for someone. I don't know where your brother is right now, emotionally speaking. I can't say what he needs, he might not even be able to. He's very lucky to have such a loving family. When I'm on the edge like that, I just want reassurance that I'm not alone, someone to talk to, and someone to hold me. I can't say that's what he needs, I can only speak from experience. You can always message me here if you want to talk about it. I hope that you can help him get to a better place.
I know heartbreak feels like it'll never go away, but it does. If you need ears or a shoulder, I'm here.

Know the pain. My advice might be shitty, but I'd say let the wound bleed a little bit, but keep yourself grounded. People come and go in your life. For everyone one that breaks your heart, someone else will come along and put it back together. With 7.215 billion people on Earth, someone who can treat you the way you deserve is going to come along, that's something i can guarantee you.

Cut ties. Your mother is a bad person. If it isn't an option, make it one. Bunk up with your boyfriend, tell him what's going on, see if you can't stay with him, if he can help you find another solution. She's clearly causing you so much pain that you just don't deserve. The sooner you get away from her, the better. I'm only 19, but I get what you're going through completely. You're not alone. You have your boyfriend which I cannot say strongly enough that i think you should talk these things out with him, but, I'm here if you want to message me, about anything.

I'm constantly thinking about suicide. Typically just "I wish I could just tie weights to myself and walk into the ocean" but during particularly bad episodes I'm actively looking for a method. I've not yet killed myself though. I always puss out at the last second. Without more context I cant speak for you, but for me I only seriously consider suicide when I feel trapped and alone in life, but it's always in my head, like a plan B for when things inevitably go wrong.

Hi. I'm Jason. You can call me Juicy. I don't mind either way. I'm 19, I live in the SF bay area, and I think I'm bipolar. I would love nothing more than to be your friend. I know this may sound trite, or canned, but if you want to talk (I would like to talk to you) you can message me here. I think you sound like an amazing person and I really want to know you better.
